newsitem.title: USA: U.S. calls on Thailand to halt return of refugees.
newsitem.headline: U.S. calls on Thailand to halt return of refugees.

text.p: The United States on Thursday demanded Thailand stop the forcible return of Karen refugees immediately, calling the situation on the Thai-Burma border "very difficult and tragic."

The refugees fled to the Thai side after recent fighting between Burmese troops and rebel Karen National Union (KNU) guerrillas, but were told they could stay only three days, after which the men would be sent back to the conflict area and the women and children to a "safe corridor" further south along the border.
State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said the United States was "deeply concerned" about the actions of the Royal Thai Army in forcibly repatriating some 900 Karen women.

"We are equally disturbed by reports that the Thai army forcibly repatriated civilian Karen males, including boys as young as 10 years old ... and denied asylum to several hundred others at the same time," he said.
Burns said the Thai government's actions ran counter to its "previous generous policy" of providing asylum to those fleeing oppression in Burma.

"We call on the Thai authorities to cease the forcible return of Karen refugees immediately and to recommence provision of asylum until conditions in Burma permit the safe and orderly return of the refugees," he said.
At the same time, Burns noted that "the ultimate responsibility for this tragedy lies with the military dictators in Burma itself" where there were "repressive policies" againt minority populations.
The KNU has been fighting the Burmese government since 1948 for greater autonomy for the Karen state.
